description:

Netflix operates our streaming service control plane on Amazon Web Services, which has led to one of the largest and most sophisticated AWS environments in the world. Cloud Security for our public cloud deployments is critical to Netflix’s security posture to protect our members, partners, employees, and intellectual property. Of this charter, the Cloud Architecture, Tooling and Security (CATS) team designs and implements strategic high-level cloud security boundaries to balance risk while enabling business needs. We provide cloud security subject matter expertise, build scalable security solutions for account management, cloud identity and access management and provide operational security services to achieve this mission.

We are looking for a cloud security engineer to join this team to serve as a critical partner in securely enabling new Netflix business verticals, supporting innovation and experimentation, and integrating new acquisitions. This role is highly collaborative, focusing on designing and implementing secure cloud access patterns, cloud security boundaries, and new paved paths, primarily involving Identity and Access Management (IAM) challenges in AWS and GCP. While not a dedicated software development role, the ability to build scrappy tooling/scripting and data analysis tools, is required for success in this Security Engineer role.

You will collaborate with software engineering teams to understand business needs and design and implement appropriate, scalable cloud security solutions. You will also design and implement new cloud security strategies and archetypes to discover, self-serve, right-size, and manage cloud resources, and develop internal tooling and scripting for GCP to build capabilities where few currently exist. Furthermore, you will perform threat assessments, apply knowledge of AWS architecture and new AWS services to address security requests, and contribute to operational excellence by reducing risks and eliminating tedious access management minutiae.

A broad and deep understanding of cloud security fundamentals, with a particular focus on CloudSec operations, AWS account management and Security Architecture

Experience collaborating with product and engineering teams to design security solutions.

•

About the Team

Netflix's Workforce Security team protects its employees, endpoints, and vendors by implementing controls for secure user access, SaaS and vendor usage, and endpoint security. The goal is to address security risks while pragmatically enabling business agility, leveraging risk-based approaches rather than policy mandates, and building strong cross-functional partnerships across the company.

About the Role

We are seeking a talented L5 Security Engineer specializing in Endpoint Security to join our team. In this role, you will be critical to identifying and managing risks across all software on Netflix endpoints. You will drive the development of scalable technical security controls that enhance business agility and reduce risk for workforce-related business scenarios.

The Workforce Security Engineer role focuses heavily on designing, implementing, and validating protective endpoint security controls. This includes developing and rolling out solutions for host hardening, vulnerability identification, and effective patch management to maintain defined security standards and prevent configuration drift across devices. Rapid genAI adoption and evolving genAI threats are changing our endpoint posture needs. A critical component of the role is designing and testing host hardening configurations for Mac, Windows, and Linux systems. You will also be responsible for designing and executing a comprehensive Patch and Vulnerability Management Strategy, enforcement, and applying Threat Intelligence to prioritize the remediation of endpoint vulnerabilities at the OS, App, and App Configuration levels.  Where necessary, you will also evaluate build vs. buy security capabilities through requirement gathering, cost-benefit analysis, and accurate estimation of development effort.

Beyond the technical implementation, this position requires strong communication and risk translation skills, specifically the ability to translate complex technical risks into clear business risks for stakeholders to inform trade-off decisions. Finally, the role includes providing standard business-hours operational support for Workforce Security and participating in infrequent 24/7 Incident Response as needed.

•

High-level familiarity with the functionality of commercially available corporate security tooling in the areas of endpoint, identity, data, and vendor security.

Ability to navigate ambiguity by taking strategic goals and decomposing them into actionable project plans

title: Software Engineer 5 - Android
description:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. The Member Experience Client Foundations team (MXCF) is responsible for building the server-driven UI (SDUI) architecture and tooling used to power the member user experience across Netflix’s iOS, Android, TV and Web client streaming applications.

The team is responsible for working closely with our server foundational partners on this SDUI architecture to ensure that we’re building holistic solutions which balance client architectural considerations across all four client platforms, alongside our server partner’s distributed system concerns.
Allowing us to deliver a flexible, scalable SDUI platform on which both our client & server product teams can deliver the innovative member experiences which Netflix sets the industry standard for.

MXCF is a foundational team. We don’t build product experiences directly. We build architecture and tooling which empowers product engineers (our customers), to build great product experiences, efficiently and reliably.
We’re currently working to evolve our SDUI architecture’s capabilities to support:

• A flexible spectrum of server-driven rendering : From coarse-grained control through to fine grained UI control; or none at all, based on product needs.

• Pushing UI updates to the client both for exceedingly high-scale needs (simultaneous concurrent updates for live events), as well user experience updates at lower scale.

• Dynamically modify the UI in response to the user’s session interaction and needs.

• Efficiently support the increasingly wide variety of content types and business verticals (shows, movies, games, ads, live, acquisition) which Netflix supports.

• Integrating generative AI into the ecosystem to increase efficiency for product engineers to utilize the platform.

The Role
This role will be focused on Android, requiring expertise with Android UI architecture and frameworks. However, we believe strong engineering aptitude transcends stacks, and providing the opportunity to explore UI development on other platforms is a unique aspect of this role.

We’re currently building solutions with Kotlin/Compose on Android, and use GraphQL as our shared data access technology. We use Swift on iOS and JavaScript/TypeScript on TV & Web.

In this role you’ll:

• Architect and build maintainable, performant Android client code with effective documentation that can be leveraged by Android developers across Netflix

• Define and drive best practices that ensure consistency, reliability, and simplicity in a high-commit-volume codebase

• Leverage modern technologies such as Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Circuit, and Dagger/Hilt, alongside GraphQL, to deliver scalable, maintainable solutions for our shared SDUI architecture

• Develop code for testability and write automated tests (JVM Unit, Espresso, Paparazzi) to uphold product quality

• Keep a pulse on cutting-edge Android technologies and software engineering practices, modernizing the codebase to accelerate innovation velocity

• Collaborate with cross-functional partners across client and server teams to define and deliver on our framework and architecture vision

• Mentor and grow less-experienced Android engineers

• Influence our framework and architecture roadmaps, and drive forward-looking technical solutions with minimal supervision

• Diverse and inclusive teams are strong teams. We encourage those with varied identities, backgrounds, and experiences to apply. We believe that creating a sense of belonging allows us to be our best selves, which in turn helps us produce our best work. We rely on our unique individual strengths to help each other grow.

• We have a distributed team across the US, while trying to maintain some pacific time overlap. With some teammates working remotely from the east coast, and some co-located in the Los Gatos, CA office. The team is committed to being ‘remote-inclusive’ and believe it’s about the work you do, and the relationships you build. Where you can best do that from is up to you.

People who do well on the team are self-motivated engineers with a passion for building solutions rooted in business and customer needs. Analytical and technical skills form a solid foundation. But more importantly, we look for engineers who understand that there are rarely any absolutes when it comes to technology. The curiosity to engage in discussions about use cases, prioritization and technical challenges with colleagues, while thoughtfully weighing trade-offs across multiple solutions is a skill we value highly. As is the desire to continually learn, grow and help your colleagues do the same.

All of this, so that Netflix members can immerse themselves in the stories they care about, on the devices they love, from whichever part of the world they call home. Without the technology behind it all ever getting in the way.
If this resonates with you, we’d love to talk!

What Sets You Apart:

• You have a deep understanding of the technical landscape of Android development and can introduce new paradigms and practices

• You're comfortable identifying opportunities and driving forward-looking technical solutions or roadmaps with little supervision

• You take a practical approach to problem-solving that considers trade-offs and avoids over-engineering, balancing business, user, and architectural needs

• You have a strong track record of leading projects and delivering results, with excellent project management and estimation skills

• You have an appreciation for diverse perspectives and a collaborative approach to problem-solving.

• You understand that it is really about solving problems. A language, framework or library choice is just a means to an end.

• You've built a track record of weaving GenAI and agentic workflows into your team's engineering practice,  not just using the tools yourself, but changing how the SDLC works for the people around you

What’s Different About Us:
Scale, Impact

Hundreds of Engineers : You’ll be improving UI development velocity for over 100 engineers...
Millions of Users : creating best-in-class streaming UIs used by over 100M users...
Thousands of Devices : across a wide spectrum of devices...
Globally : in almost every country in the world.

Unique Technical Challenges
We build framework solutions (libraries, architectures, and tools) which are flexible enough to span a variety of product use cases, across a varied client, server and network performance landscape, all while being easy to use for the engineers we support. The breadth of problems we work on provide a great career opportunity to explore different technical areas and deepen your expertise.

Collaboration and Communication
It’s not all about the tech. We highly value the skills required to build strong relationships and collaborate effectively.

Responsibility and Ownership
We believe in hiring responsible engineers, providing them with the business context they need, and then freeing them up to own their project’s scope, design, trade-offs, and figure out the implementation details.

title: Analytics Engineer 5 - Identity & Signal
description:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

In 2022 we launched a new lower-priced, ad-supported tier, and we are building an in-house, world-class ad-tech ecosystem to give our members more choice and to offer advertisers a premium, better-than-linear-TV experience. We are looking for the founding members of this new business area for Netflix.

The Identity & Signals team builds the identity foundation of the Netflix ads business — the graph and matching systems that let us recognize the same person or household across signals, devices, and partner data sources, and that determine which signals we can responsibly and accurately use for targeting, measurement, and reporting. We build and maintain the identity graph, run and evaluate entity-matching and resolution pipelines, and manage relationships with identity providers so that advertisers and internal teams can trust the signals underneath every campaign.

This is a foundational role on a small, high-leverage team. You will build the analytics and data infrastructure that powers identity matching and graph construction — designing the tables, pipelines, and metrics that let the team and its stakeholders understand match quality, coverage, and drift over time. You'll work end-to-end: from raw signal ingestion, through matching logic and graph construction, to the dashboards and data products that make identity health visible and actionable across the company.

In this role, you will:

- Design, build, and maintain the data models and pipelines that support identity graph construction, entity matching, and identity resolution across first-party and third-party signals.

- Partner with data engineering and software engineering to productionize matching logic, ensuring pipelines are scalable, well-tested, and monitored for data quality and drift.

- Build metrics, dashboards, and analytics that quantify match rate, match quality, coverage, and graph stability, and that surface anomalies before they affect downstream campaigns.

- Work closely with data science to evaluate and improve matching algorithms, providing the clean, well-documented data and features needed to test and iterate on models.

- Manage and evaluate the analytics relationship with external identity providers (e.g., Experian, TransUnion, LiveRamp), including onboarding new sources, validating match performance, and monitoring ongoing data quality.

- Translate identity graph and matching concepts — nodes, edges, match confidence, deterministic vs. probabilistic matching — into clear, actionable insights for product, sales, and other non-technical stakeholders.

- Collaborate with product and cross-functional partners to define identity requirements, evaluate trade-offs (accuracy vs. coverage vs. privacy), and prioritize roadmap work.

- Communicate technical decisions, trade-offs, and results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences at all levels of the company.

We are looking for:

- 5+ years of experience as an analytics engineer, data engineer, or similar role working with large-scale data.

- Experience working with graph data structures and graph-based data models (e.g., property graphs, graph databases, or graph analytics on top of relational/columnar stores).

- Familiarity with entity matching / identity resolution concepts — deterministic and probabilistic matching, fuzzy matching, blocking/candidate generation, and match quality evaluation.

- Knowledge of, or direct experience working with, identity providers such as Experian, TransUnion, LiveRamp, or similar data/identity partners.

- Strong SQL and Python skills, with experience building and maintaining production data pipelines.

- Experience designing data models, metrics, and dashboards that make complex technical systems understandable to non-technical stakeholders.

- Demonstrated ability to collaborate closely across data engineering, software engineering, data science, and product teams.

- Ability to work independently, drive your own projects, and make compelling cases for prioritization.

- Embodies the Netflix values while bringing a new perspective to continue improving our culture.

Nice to have:

- Experience with ad-tech identity concepts — cross-device identity, household graphs, cookie/ID deprecation, or media measurement.

- Experience with graph databases or graph-processing frameworks (e.g., Neo4j, Neptune, GraphFrames, or similar).

- Familiarity with our ML/data stack (Metaflow) or comparable large-scale data tooling.

- Experience working with privacy-sensitive data and an understanding of relevant data governance and privacy considerations for identity data.

- Experience applying GenAI to boost developer/analytics productivity.

Ultimately, we make data- and AI-driven product development faster, safer, and more dependable at scale so teams can focus on building great experiences that entertain the world.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a highly technical Product Manager to lead Data Developer & Analytics Experiences within the Analytics Platform & Experiences team.

Your primary mission is to deliver a unified, AI-native experience that spans how practitioners build data assets, build and operate data agents, and orchestrate data workflows at scale. On the Data Developer side, you will own the practitioner “inner loop”; SQL and Python-first code authoring in AI-native IDEs (Cursor, Claude Code, JupyterLab), Python libraries, lifecycle and CLI tooling, data quality tooling, and the developer experience for building data agents that can securely discover, query, and act on data. Analytics engineers, data engineers, and data scientists will be your primary customers, with a focus on making it easier for them to build data assets, orchestrate reliable workflows, and develop data agents. Partnering closely with engineering, design, and data leaders, you will shape product direction and deliver impactful capabilities across developer productivity, workflow orchestration, data quality and observability, and AI-native development.

In this role, you will shape the future of Data Developer Experiences and Workflow Orchestration at Netflix by leading a high-impact product portfolio. You will operate with significant autonomy to set strategic direction, define multi-year roadmaps, and make high-leverage tradeoffs across developer productivity, workflow orchestration, reliability and observability, data quality, and AI-native development—including how practitioners build and operate data agents.

What makes this role exciting is the blend of strategic vision and hands-on leadership. Your success will be measured by enabling Netflix's growth, innovation, and competitive advantage, while delighting users with exceptional experiences that empower teams to work more efficiently and with greater satisfaction.

Set Direction: Develop a compelling long-term vision and strategy for your portfolio, aligning user needs with business objectives and industry trends for the Analytics Experiences.

Champion Users: Build deep user understanding and empathy through regular engagement, research, and feedback loops to identify pain points and opportunities.

Guide Development: Partner with design and engineering to define requirements, create intuitive interfaces, and validate solutions that ensure cohesive user journeys across the platform ecosystem.

•
Support Architecture: Partner with engineering on critical architecture decisions that ensure platform sustainability, scalability, and flexibility while strategically managing technical debt.

•
Drive Adoption: Create effective rollout strategies and promote new capabilities through targeted communication, education, and roadshows, while providing comprehensive documentation, learning resources, and self-service tools that accelerate adoption and reduce support burden.

•
Drive Improvement: Define success metrics centered on user delight and productivity gains, and implement tracking to continuously improve platform capabilities through data-informed experiments.

•

•

We value candidates who can balance strategic thinking with tactical execution, technical depth with user empathy, and decisive leadership with collaborative partnership. This role requires someone who thrives in ambiguity, can navigate complex technical and organizational landscapes, and ultimately delivers significant impact for your users and Netflix as a whole.

Technical Excellence

•
Expertise: 8+ years of Technical Product Management experience (or equivalent technical role) in complex technical domains. Comfortable discussing technical design trade-offs and system quality attributes with engineering teams.

•
Domain Knowledge: Strong knowledge of modern analytics architectures and data developer tooling — including dbt-based transformation workflows, workflow orchestration and scheduling, and deep familiarity with the practitioner stack: IDEs and notebooks (Cursor, JupyterLab, VS Code), Python/SQL developer tooling, interactive compute environments, and data quality/observability frameworks.

Product Leadership

Strategic Vision: Proven track record of managing product portfolios in complex technical domains with clear vision and strategy to maximize portfolio impact. Skilled at connecting business objectives with user needs, balancing quick wins with strategic bets, and making thoughtful trade-offs.

•
Customer Obsession: Deeply understands user needs through continuous engagement. Exceptional at identifying and articulating clear problem statements. Develops innovative solutions with strong product intuition and taste, thinking holistically about end-to-end user experience.

•
Business Acumen: Understands how platform investments drive business outcomes. Articulates the ROI of technical investments in business terms and connects platform capabilities to Netflix's strategic priorities. Balances technical excellence with business pragmatism.

Data Driven: Deeply analytical mindset that leverages quantitative and qualitative data to understand user behavior, validate assumptions, and inform product decisions. Builds a metrics-driven culture with clear success metrics to measure impact and drive continuous improvement.

description:

Where Talent Knowledge Stands Today

Across Talent, content ownership is scattered: GBPs (Global Business Practices, which are our centers of excellence) each own their own employee-facing content, and Employee Services owns their own FAQs and work instructions. Much of it lives on the Netflix Knowledge Platform (NKP), the system that hosts these sites, including the Netflix Resource Center (NRC), Talent's employee-facing intranet, with more business lines migrating over time. But the NKP doesn't belong to Talent, and a growing stack of system documentation lives outside it entirely. This role governs all of it, on the NKP and off, while our technology partner team owns the platform itself.

This is a founding role. You'd be the first to own knowledge governance for Talent, with a genuine greenfield to shape: building the shared taxonomy, the review lifecycle, the cross-GBP forum where these groups align, and the AI-readiness plan that makes this content work with the search tools employees reach for first. You get to define what good looks like from the ground up.

The Role

This is part strategist, part librarian. You'll own the governance model, content standards, taxonomy, and indexing for Talent's knowledge estate, on the NKP and off, and you'll shape the longer-term strategy for how that knowledge supports the company at scale. Day-to-day, that means balancing hands-on knowledge operations (structure, tagging, findability) with the strategic work of defining how governance should function across Talent. You'll also be the bridge between Talent's content and the AI tools that surface it, understanding how search and retrieval consume knowledge and staying ahead of where those tools are heading so our content is built for them rather than catching up. That includes designing workflows where AI can proactively surface content gaps and produce first-draft material.

Because Talent has never had this function, a big part of the job is influence without authority: the GBP leads who own the content don't report to you, so getting standards adoption is a constant, active push. The role comes with an executive sponsor (the Talent Tech & Operations Senior Director) and a leadership-endorsed mandate, so adoption is expected and backed from above rather than something you generate alone, and part of the job is building and sustaining that senior-leader alignment as the model evolves. You'll also define and build the team this function needs, like editors and other roles as the work demands.

Responsibilities Include, But Are Not Limited To

•
Design and own Talent's content governance strategy and operating rhythms: the standards, content lifecycle, longer-term vision, and the recurring reviews that keep each live NKP site's content and standards current, all applied by GBPs, their stewards, and Employee Services to their own content

•
Own the taxonomy, information architecture, and indexing for the Netflix Resource Center and the wider Talent knowledge estate, so content is organized, discoverable, and usable across Talent

•
Make Talent's knowledge AI-ready and keep it that way as the tools evolve: structure content (metadata, tagging, chunking, consistent Q&A formatting, no stale duplicates) for accurate retrieval, and stay ahead of how AI search consumes content so the estate is built for where those tools are heading

•

Our Team

Our team is new yet faces the enormous ambition of building highly performant advertising systems and delivering high impact to our business by monetizing our incredible slate of content. As one of the newest entrants in the rapidly growing Connected TV advertising space, we seek to build unique value propositions that help us differentiate from the competition and become a market leader in record time.

The Ads Platform Engineering org builds advertising systems and integrations that power ad delivery using our world-class content delivery ecosystem. We use a number of Netflix investments and innovations to power our ads, a unique mix of client and server-side ad insertions, state-of-the-art content delivery systems, ad encoding recipes, content understanding and metadata, and more. We deliver ads in a manner that's thoughtful of our members' viewing experience and drive great outcomes for advertisers.

The Account Foundations team owns the accounts domain for Netflix Ads, i.e the system that defines who our advertisers are, what they're eligible for, and how they transact. It sounds like table stakes, but we don't have a lot of the moving pieces in place yet. Today, account data is scattered across systems, hierarchies are incomplete, and too much of what should be automated is still done manually. Every team building on top of advertiser data, such as sales workflows, media planning, programmatic integrations, and packaging, runs into these gaps. Our job is to fix that from the ground up and make sure it doesn't become a problem again, as the business scales.

We're working across four areas:

•
Core Accounts: We're rebuilding the account data model that can actually represent how advertisers and agencies are structured in the real world, representing HoldCo hierarchies, brand relationships, and multi-tier agency structures with strong governance being enforced. This also enables the creation of externalized APIs, allowing advertisers and agencies to view and manage their accounts as we move into a world of agenctic buying.

•
Account Intelligence: We're building the enrichment layer to identify who our advertisers are, where they spend their advertising budget, how they're structured, and whether our internal data matches reality.

•
Account Cohort and Verification Automation: Cohort assignment and identity verification are both manual today and both scale linearly with advertiser growth. Handling these problems at scale in an automated manner will be one of the key drivers of our long term success.

•
Spend Attribution: We are building an automated attribution engine to accurately map programmatic spend from DSPs and map it with the corresponding advertisers, agencies, and ad accounts across supply channels.

The work is foundational, which means it's both high leverage and high stakes, as well as a truly zero-to-one space. The architectural decisions we make now will be load-bearing for every team in Netflix Ads for years. If you're drawn to problems where getting the architecture right the first time actually matters, this is the team for you.

We are looking for highly motivated engineers working in the advertising space who are excited to join us on this journey.

Open Connect (OC) is a critical group within Netflix that builds and manages a content delivery network (CDN) that delivers all of Netflix’s streaming video. In addition to streaming video, we work on projects within Netflix that leverage physical infrastructure, such as our Cloud Games and Live initiatives. According to a 2023 Sandvine report, data delivered by OC accounts for approximately 15% of all downstream traffic volume across the entire internet. Most of this traffic is delivered by our edge cache servers.

A small team of talented software engineers develops and maintains the operating system and platform that run the content caches. These appliances run a heterogeneous, deeply integrated stack, including Linux, FreeBSD, firmware, BMC, FPGAs, BIOS/UEFI, and containers. Because of the important role these caches serve, it is critical that they be both efficient and secure from the hardware up.

We are looking for a Security Software Engineer to architect and implement system-level security for the OC edge and gaming appliances, serving as the in-house home for hardware and low-level OS security assurance, with the opportunity to directly impact a critical area of the business.

•
Implement security enhancements using a variety of methods such as kernel and user-space development, configuration changes, or leveraging hardware-based security features such as TPMs and hardware offload.

•

•

•
Partner with stakeholders in different organizations to build secure architecture for binary ingestion and execution..

We are looking for the founding members of this new business area for Netflix.

The Ads Forecasting team builds the predictive foundation of the Netflix ads business — the models that tell us, before a campaign ever runs, how much inventory is available and how a campaign will deliver. We forecast supply and demand across audiences, ad products, and formats, and we predict campaign outcomes such as maximum availability, delivery confidence, reach, and frequency, accounting for the ad-serving optimizations that shape delivery. Our forecasts power media planning, underwriting, budget planning, yield, and the public API.

This is a brand-new, foundational role. You will build the machine learning models that augment our simulation-based engine for predicting campaign delivery — turning a slow, rules-based simulation into fast, accurate, learnable models of how campaigns deliver against real inventory. You'll own the modeling and prototyping end-to-end and partner closely with our ML engineering team to take models to production.

In this role, you will:

•
Build, prototype, and iterate on supervised machine learning models that predict campaign delivery outcomes — delivery risk, reach, frequency, and contention — to replace the current simulation engine.

•
Model demand-side campaign outcomes while incorporating supply-side signals, so the models reason about how well available inventory matches what advertisers are trying to achieve (targeting, frequency caps, contention, pacing).

•
Design rigorous offline and online evaluation frameworks to measure model accuracy, robustness to seasonality and distribution shift, and lift over the simulation baseline.

•
Own feature engineering and contribute to the team's feature store — turning ad-serving logs, campaign attributes, and supply signals into reusable, well-documented features.

•
Prioritize explainability and interpretability: your models' outputs must be defensible to sales and media-planning stakeholders making real booking and underwriting decisions.

Collaborate with cross-functional partners across product, engineering, and sales to define objectives, constraints, and trade-offs, and to drive adoption of ML-driven forecasts.

•
Communicate technical decisions, trade-offs, and results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences at all levels of the company.

We are looking for:

•
Advanced degree (PhD or Master's) in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field.

•
5+ years of relevant experience building machine learning models on large-scale data.

•
Deep expertise in supervised learning (e.g. gradient-boosted trees, regression, and related methods) with a strong bias toward interpretable, explainable models.

•
Strong feature engineering skills and familiarity with feature stores and standard ML lifecycle practice (versioning, evaluation, monitoring, retraining).

•
Proven ability to prototype algorithms and validate them rigorously against production data.

•
Strong programming skills in Python and strong SQL.

•
Working knowledge of ad-serving and campaign concepts — how campaigns are delivered and what creates delivery risk: targeting, frequency caps, contention, bidding, pacing, budget planning, and the core campaign objects/attributes; and the metrics that matter (reach, frequency, impressions, clicks, outcomes). description:

The Open Connect Infrastructure Capacity Planning team plays a central role in ensuring that our members and internal customers consistently enjoy a seamless experience, achieved through the timely deployment and ongoing management of Netflix’s owned infrastructure capacity. Our team is dedicated to the development of long-range capacity forecasts that are forward-looking, adaptable to rapidly evolving product needs, and focused on efficiency. We collaborate closely with a diverse range of cross-functional stakeholders to understand their current and future infrastructure requirements and make strategic recommendations around product implementation and design. Some of our team’s core responsibilities include:

•
Development of Long-Range Infrastructure Capacity Strategies: Create forward-looking strategies that inform long-term financial planning, network design, and near-term deployment and implementation decisions.

•
Effective Infrastructure Allocation: Convert demand forecasts across multiple products into clear, actionable capacity plans and strategic recommendations to drive investment decisions. Balance infrastructure availability across product types.

•
Data-Driven Analyses for Platform Optimization and Scalability: Conduct ongoing, data-driven analyses focused on optimizing efficiency, spend, and architectural direction while ensuring long-term platform scalability and resiliency.

•
Risk Assessment & Management: Identification of potential risks related to capacity shortages or excesses and development of mitigation strategies.

•
Infrastructure Performance Monitoring: Continuous tracking of infrastructure performance and utilization to identify bottlenecks or inefficiencies.

What You'll Do

The Open Connect Capacity Planning team is a centralized group positioned at the intersection of business strategy and implementation. Our mission is to strategically recommend, build, and maintain the right type and quantity of capacity in the right locations and at the right times to ensure high-quality service, efficiency, scalability, and resilience for Netflix and our ISP partners. The primary objectives include developing and executing infra capacity plans, providing technical expertise to leaders, analyzing data to inform capacity decisions, and driving long-term capacity roadmap planning. You will be partnering with stunning colleagues within Product & Technology Engineering organization to assess strategic initiatives, develop actionable insights, and drive operational analytics to inform short term and long term infrastructure strategy for Open connect. This is an individual contributor role that is expected to work with limited supervision on strategic thinking, problem solving, and running cross-functional stakeholder relationships and initiatives.  Some of your primary responsibilities include:

•
Translate demand signals (including bandwidth, storage, and network capacity requirements) into actionable capacity forecasts, both short-term and long-term, to inform infrastructure investment and scaling strategies.

•
Conduct what-if analysis and hypothesis testing to assess capacity impacts and trade-offs driven by specific demand signals and product requirements; present outcomes, insights, risks, and potential mitigations, and define key metrics to support strategic investment and prioritization decisions for leadership, finance, and Engineering & Architecture teams.

•
Orchestrate the timely implementation and allocation of infrastructure augments in coordination with deployment and operational  teams.

•
Collaborate cross-functionally with product managers, Product, Finance & Strategy, TPMs, Engineers, and the Partnerships team to support scaling strategies for new product launches, especially those related to Studio Infrastructure.

•
Develop requirements for modeling and automation tools, continuously evaluating and enhancing workflows, processes, and tools to minimize time spent on modeling and maximize focus on delivering impactful insights, storytelling, and business outcomes.

•
Manage risks and help prioritize competing efforts among stakeholder and implementation teams by evaluating trade-offs, providing objective recommendations, and constructively pushing back when necessary, including asking whether the potential benefits justify the required effort and spend, to ensure informed decision-making that aligns with organizational goals and business priorities.

Who will be successful in this role?

•
A deeply analytical individual who leverages quantitative methods, statistical tools, and massive datasets to guide capacity choices, utilizing scenario-based and hypothesis-driven models while maintaining objective skepticism in ambiguous situations.

•
A forward-looking planner capable of modeling long-range requirements (5+ years) to ensure platform scalability and create proactive solutions for shared infrastructure across multiple products.

•
